unit.title: Comply with the occupational health and safety, security and hygiene practices

theory1.instructions: Answer all 45 questions. Each question has one best answer: choose it. Each question is worth 1 mark. Time allowed: 2 hours 30 minutes. Your answers are saved as you go.

questions.stem: Who has a duty to keep a hotel workplace safe?
options: Only the hotel's general manager
Only the guests staying at the hotel
Only the government's safety inspectors
Both the employer and every worker

questions.stem: What is a worker's main duty under health and safety rules?
options: Fix every electrical fault in the building on their own
Work safely, follow the rules and report hazards
Buy all of their own safety equipment
Decide which safety rules they will follow

questions.stem: What is a hazard?
options: Anything that could cause harm
An accident that has already happened
A report written after an injury
A sign that warns of a wet floor

questions.stem: In health and safety, what is a "risk"?
options: A list of everything in the first-aid kit
The name of the safety officer
The chance of harm, and how bad it could be
Any object that is coloured red

questions.stem: What is the best way to deal with a hazard, if it can be done?
options: Put up a small sign
Give everyone gloves
Remove it completely
Tell guests to be careful

questions.stem: Why is PPE (personal protective equipment) thought of as the last line of defence?
options: It only protects the wearer, and only if used right
It is the cheapest control, so it is used first
It removes the hazard completely from the workplace for good
It is only needed when an inspector visits

questions.stem: Which PPE should a room attendant wear when cleaning a toilet with a chemical cleaner?
options: Cotton gloves and a paper hat
A hairnet and open sandals
No PPE, as long as she works quickly
Rubber gloves, and eye protection if the label says

questions.stem: Why should kitchen staff wear closed, non-slip shoes?
options: Because they look smarter to guests than any other shoes
To stop slips and protect feet from hot spills
So they can run faster around the kitchen
So guests can hear staff coming

questions.stem: What is the safe way to lift a box of linen from the floor?
options: Bend over at the waist with straight legs and lift it quickly
Bend your knees, keep your back straight and the load close
Twist your body as you lift, to save time
Hold the box at arm's length away from your body

questions.stem: A box of drinks for the villa bar is too heavy for one person. What should you do?
options: Drag it across the floor
Lift it alone, but quickly
Get help or use a trolley
Leave it in the doorway

questions.stem: You have just mopped the hotel lobby floor. What must you put out?
options: A lost property box
A fire blanket
A guest comment card
A wet floor sign

questions.stem: A delivery box has been left in a staff corridor where people walk. What should you do?
options: Move it to its proper place, or report it
Step over it each time and carry on with your work
Cover it with a sheet so that it is easier to see
Leave it, as it is not your box

questions.stem: Where do you find full information on a chemical's hazards, first aid and safe storage?
options: On its SDS, from the supplier
On the supplier's delivery receipt or invoice
On the hotel restaurant's menu
In the guest welcome book

questions.stem: Why must bleach never be mixed with ammonia or with acid toilet cleaners?
options: It makes the bleach work much better
It turns the cleaner a bright colour
It gives off a dangerous, toxic gas
It makes the mix smell more pleasant

questions.stem: A cleaning chemical has to be diluted before use. How should you do this?
options: Add extra so it works faster
Measure it as the label says
Guess the amount by the colour
Mix it with another cleaner

questions.stem: A cleaning chemical splashes into a co-worker's eye. What should you do first?
options: Rub the eye hard with a cloth to remove the chemical
Put a cold drink can against the eye
Cover the eye and send them back to work
Flush it with plenty of clean water and get help

questions.stem: What three things does a fire need to start and keep burning (the fire triangle)?
options: Smoke, water and wind
Gas, sparks and metal
Light, sound and heat
Heat, fuel and oxygen

questions.stem: A pan of cooking oil catches fire on the stove. What should you do, if it is safe to?
options: Turn off the heat and cover the pan to cut off the air
Throw a jug of water over it
Carry the burning pan outside
Fan the flames to blow them out

questions.stem: Which fire extinguisher is suitable for a fire in a computer at the front desk?
options: Water, sprayed at the screen
Foam, sprayed at the base
Carbon dioxide (CO2)
Wet chemical, for cooking oil

questions.stem: When the fire alarm sounds in the hotel, what should staff do?
options: Finish the task they are doing first, then go and look
Leave by the nearest safe exit, as the fire plan says
Use the lift so that they get out more quickly
Go back to the locker room for their bag

questions.stem: Why must fire exits and escape routes never be blocked, even by a linen trolley for a few minutes?
options: People must be able to get out fast in a fire
Fire inspectors may come by to check them at any time
Trolleys are not allowed in corridors
Guests do not like seeing trolleys

questions.stem: A kettle in a villa has a frayed cord. What should you do?
options: Wrap the frayed part with sticky tape
Keep using it, but only when your hands are dry
Stop using it, label it faulty and report it
Put it back for the next guest to use

questions.stem: Why should you never touch electrical switches or plugs with wet hands?
options: Water makes the switch rust overnight
Wet hands leave marks on the plates
It will make the fuse blow every time
Water conducts electricity and can cause a shock

questions.stem: A room attendant smells gas in a villa kitchen. What should she do?
options: Switch on the lights and the fan to look for the leak
Do not use switches, open windows, leave and report
Light a match to find where it comes from
Spray air freshener and carry on cleaning

questions.stem: A cook burns her hand on a hot tray. What is the correct first aid?
options: Put butter or toothpaste on it at once
Cool it under cool running water for about 20 minutes
Burst any blisters to let them drain
Wrap it tightly in a dry towel

questions.stem: Why should a worker cover a small cut on the hand before handling food?
options: So the cut heals faster in the heat
So that nobody can see the cut
Because a plaster helps the gloves fit better
To keep germs from the cut out of the food

questions.stem: A guest slips by the villa pool but says they are fine. What should you do?
options: Check they are OK, get first aid if needed and report it
Nothing, since the guest said they are fine
Ask the guest to sign a form saying it was their own fault
Tell co-workers but not the supervisor

questions.stem: Why should an incident where someone was nearly hurt be reported, even if nobody was injured?
options: So the worker who was involved can be punished for it
Because it counts towards a staff bonus
So the cause can be fixed before someone is hurt
It does not need to be reported at all

questions.stem: A hurricane warning is given for the area. Which is a correct step for a villa team?
options: Follow the hurricane plan and secure loose items
Open all the windows so the wind can pass through
Carry on as normal until the storm arrives
Send all staff home and leave the guests alone

questions.stem: During an earthquake, what should staff and guests who are indoors do?
options: Run outside down the stairs at once
Stand inside the lift
Stand next to a window
Drop, cover and hold on

questions.stem: A person at the front desk says they have lost their room key and asks for a new one. What must you do first?
options: Give them a new key, because they seem polite and honest
Tell them the room number out loud
Check their identity against the registration
Give them the master key for now

questions.stem: A caller asks which room a guest is staying in. What should you do?
options: Give the room number, as the caller knows the name
Offer to connect the call, without giving the number
Read out the guest's full booking details to the caller
Ask another guest to pass the message on

questions.stem: Why must master keys be signed out and never lent to anyone?
options: They are very costly to cut again
They are heavy to carry around
Only managers like to use them
They open many rooms, so a lost key puts guests at risk

questions.stem: A room attendant finds a stranger with no key inside a guest's room. What should she do?
options: Stay calm, do not confront them, and call security
Lock the stranger inside the room until the manager comes
Fight the stranger to get them out
Carry on cleaning the next room

questions.stem: You see an unattended bag in the hotel lobby that nobody claims. What should you do?
options: Open it to find the owner's name
Do not touch it; report it to security
Carry it to the lost property room straight away
Throw it in the large bin outside

questions.stem: A guest's ring is found while cleaning a room after check-out. What should happen?
options: Keep it, as the guest has already left
Leave it on the bed for the next guest
Log it and hand it in to lost property
Give it to a co-worker to look after

questions.stem: When must food handlers wash their hands?
options: Only at the start of each shift
Only when their hands look dirty
Before work and after each dirty task
Only after they eat their lunch

questions.stem: A cook has had diarrhoea and vomiting. What should she do?
options: Stay off work and tell the supervisor
Come in to work, but wear gloves for the whole shift
Work only on cold food today
Take medicine and say nothing

questions.stem: At what temperature should cold food be kept, or as the Centre's food safety plan says?
options: 10 °C or below
15 °C or below
20 °C or below
5 °C or below

questions.stem: Why are raw meat and ready-to-eat foods kept apart?
options: So that the two kinds of food cool down at different speeds
To stop germs passing from raw to ready-to-eat food
Because raw meat takes up too much space
So that the fridge door closes easily

questions.stem: A room attendant finds a used needle in a guest's bin. What should she do?
options: Pick it up carefully with her fingers
Push it down further into the bin
Wrap it in a towel and put it in the linen bag on the trolley
Use tongs to put it in a sharps box, and report it

questions.stem: What should be worn to clean up vomit or blood in a guest room?
options: Disposable gloves and an apron
Bare hands, washed well after
Cotton gloves from the linen room
A face towel held in the hand

questions.stem: Room attendants and cooks work in the heat. Which habit helps prevent heat illness?
options: Drink only energy drinks during the shift
Work faster to finish before midday
Drink water often and take breaks somewhere cool
Drink less water so that you need fewer toilet breaks

questions.stem: Pool chlorine is stored at a villa. Which is safe practice?
options: Store it in the kitchen cupboard, next to the guests' food
Keep it cool, dry and away from other chemicals
Pour it into empty drink bottles
Keep it in the sun to stop it getting damp

questions.stem: You need to dust a high shelf in a villa. What should you stand on?
options: A swivel office chair
A stack of boxes
The edge of the bathtub
A step ladder in good condition

theory2.instructions: Section A has 15 short answers (2 marks each). Section B has 10 essay questions (5 marks each): answer each in full sentences. Time allowed: 3 hours 35 minutes. Your answers are saved as you go.

shortAnswers.stem: What item, made of fire-resistant cloth and kept in a quick-release holder, is used to smother a small pan fire?
What is the name of the safe place outside where everyone gathers after leaving the building in a fire?
When using a fire extinguisher, people remember PASS. What does the first P stand for?
What do the letters SDS stand for, on the sheet that comes with a cleaning chemical?
What is the term for an incident in which nobody was hurt, but someone could have been?
What colour of plaster is used in kitchens, so that it is easy to see if it falls into food?
What is the name for the range of temperatures between 5 °C and 63 °C, where germs in food grow fastest?
To about what core temperature, in °C, should poultry be cooked, checked with a clean probe thermometer, or as the Centre's food safety plan says?
Health guides say you should scrub your hands with soap for at least how many seconds?
What do the letters CCTV stand for, as used for security cameras in a hotel?
What is the word for the planned, orderly way of getting everyone out of a building in an emergency?
What is the term for locking a faulty machine's switch off and fixing a warning label to it, so that nobody can use it?
Which telephone number do you call in Jamaica for the fire brigade or an ambulance?
What do the letters FIFO stand for, in using older stock first so that food does not go out of date?
Which fuel, used for stoves and water heaters in many villas, is stored in cylinders and is heavier than air, so that a leak collects low down?

essays.stem: Explain the duties of the employer and of each worker for health and safety in a hotel or villa.
essays.modelAnswer: The employer must provide a safe place of work and safe ways of working. This includes keeping the building, equipment and electrical items in good repair, and giving the right PPE, safe chemicals with their safety data sheets, training and supervision, first-aid kits, fire equipment and clear emergency plans. The employer should find hazards, assess the risks and put controls in place, and record and look into accidents. Each worker must take care of their own safety and the safety of co-workers and guests. A worker must follow the safety rules and the training they have been given, use PPE correctly, use equipment only as they were shown, and never remove guards or misuse safety equipment. They must report hazards, faults, accidents and near misses to the supervisor at once, and must not come to work under the influence of alcohol or drugs. Both sides work together, for example at staff briefings or on a safety committee, and both follow the law and the property's own rules.
markingPoints: Employer provides a safe workplace, equipment and safe ways of working
Employer gives PPE, training, supervision, first aid and emergency plans
Employer assesses risks, and records and looks into accidents
Worker follows the rules and training, and uses PPE and equipment correctly
Worker reports hazards, faults, accidents and near misses, and works with the employer on safety

essays.stem: Describe the steps of a simple risk assessment for a task such as cleaning a villa bathroom, with examples of hazards and controls.
essays.modelAnswer: A risk assessment is a careful look at what could cause harm, so that it can be prevented. Step 1 is to find the hazards. In a villa bathroom these include wet, slippery floors, cleaning chemicals, broken glass or razors left by guests, bending and reaching, and electrical items such as a hair dryer near water. Step 2 is to decide who might be harmed and how: the room attendant could slip, get a chemical burn or a cut, and a guest could slip on a wet floor. Step 3 is to judge the risk, by thinking how likely the harm is and how bad it could be, and then to choose controls. Controls could be: dilute chemicals as the label says and never mix them; wear rubber gloves; put out a wet floor sign and dry the floor; pick up sharps with tongs into a sharps box; and use a long-handled brush instead of kneeling. Step 4 is to write down the findings and tell the team. Step 5 is to review the assessment when something changes or after an accident.
markingPoints: Finds the hazards, with suitable bathroom examples
Decides who could be harmed and how
Judges the risk (how likely and how bad)
Chooses suitable controls, with examples
Records the findings, tells the team and reviews the assessment

essays.stem: Describe how to lift and carry a heavy load safely, such as a full laundry bag or a case of drinks, and how to avoid back injury.
essays.modelAnswer: Before lifting, I think about the load and the route. I check how heavy the load is by testing one corner, and whether I can carry it alone. If it is too heavy or awkward, I split it into smaller loads, get a co-worker to help, or use a trolley. I clear the route of obstacles and make sure doors are open. To lift, I stand close to the load with my feet apart, one slightly forward. I bend my knees, keep my back straight and get a firm grip. I lift smoothly with my leg muscles, keeping the load close to my body, and I do not jerk. I look ahead, not down, and turn by moving my feet, never by twisting my back. I put the load down by bending my knees again. In a team lift, one person gives the commands. To avoid back injury, I also do not overfill laundry bags, I keep heavy items on low shelves, and I report any pain early.
markingPoints: Assesses the load and plans the route first
Uses help, a trolley or smaller loads when needed
Correct posture: feet apart, knees bent, back straight, firm grip
Keeps the load close, lifts smoothly, and turns with the feet without twisting
Prevention: not overfilling bags, heavy items low, team lifts and reporting pain early

essays.stem: Explain how to handle, use and store cleaning chemicals safely in housekeeping.
essays.modelAnswer: Before using a chemical, I read the label and the safety data sheet (SDS), which tell me the hazards, the PPE needed, the first aid and how to store it. I wear the PPE the label asks for, usually rubber gloves, and eye protection for strong products. I dilute the chemical exactly as the label says, using a measuring jug, and I follow the maker's instructions. I never mix products, especially bleach with ammonia or acid cleaners, because this gives off a toxic gas. I work with the windows open or the fan on, for good airflow. I keep chemicals in their original labelled containers, or in correctly labelled spray bottles, and never in drink bottles. On the trolley, chemicals are kept away from clean linen and guest supplies, and the trolley is never left where children can reach it. Chemicals are stored in a cool, dry, locked store, off the floor and away from food. Spills are cleaned up at once, as the SDS says, and reported.
markingPoints: Reads the label and the SDS before use
Wears the right PPE and works with good airflow
Dilutes exactly as the label says and never mixes products
Keeps chemicals in original or correctly labelled containers, never in drink bottles
Stores them safely (cool, dry, locked, away from food and linen); spills cleaned up and reported

essays.stem: Describe what you would do if you discovered a fire in a hotel, and explain how fire risks are prevented.
essays.modelAnswer: If I discovered a fire, I would raise the alarm at once by shouting "Fire!" and using the nearest fire alarm point, and make sure the fire brigade is called on 110, as the hotel's fire plan says. I would only try to put out a small fire if I have been trained, it is safe, and I have a clear way out behind me, using the right extinguisher: carbon dioxide for electrical fires, and a fire blanket or wet chemical extinguisher for cooking oil, never water on oil. If the fire is growing, I would leave, closing doors behind me to slow it down. I would help guests to leave by the nearest safe exit, never use the lift, and go to the assembly point for the roll call. I would not go back in for any reason. To prevent fires, staff keep exits and corridors clear, report faulty wiring and equipment, never overload sockets, keep cooking areas and extraction hoods free of grease, store chemicals and gas safely, and take part in fire drills.
markingPoints: Raises the alarm and makes sure the fire brigade is called
Only tackles a small fire if trained and safe, with the right extinguisher (never water on oil)
Closes doors, and helps guests out by the nearest safe exit without using lifts
Goes to the assembly point for the roll call and does not go back in
Prevention: clear exits, faults reported, no overloaded sockets, clean hoods, safe storage, drills

essays.stem: Explain what a worker should do after an accident at work, from first aid to reporting it.
essays.modelAnswer: First I would make the area safe, for example by switching off a machine or putting out a wet floor sign, so that nobody else is hurt. I would check the injured person and call the trained first aider. If the injury is serious, such as heavy bleeding, a bad burn, a head injury, or the person is unconscious, I would make sure an ambulance is called on 110 at once, asking someone else to call while I stay with the person. I would give only the first aid I have been trained to give, for example cooling a burn under cool running water, and wear gloves if there is blood. I would keep the person calm and not move them if they may have a back or neck injury. When the person has been cared for, I would tell the supervisor and fill in the accident report: the date, time and place, what happened, who was hurt and how, who saw it, and what first aid was given. The report helps the property find the cause and stop it happening again.
markingPoints: Makes the area safe first
Calls the first aider, and an ambulance for a serious injury
Gives only trained first aid, with gloves for blood, and does not move someone with a possible back or neck injury
Tells the supervisor and fills in the accident report with full details
Explains that reporting helps find the cause and prevent a repeat

essays.stem: Describe the security practices that protect guests, their belongings and their privacy in a hotel or villa.
essays.modelAnswer: Guests must feel safe, so every staff member has a part in security. At the front desk, I never say a guest's room number aloud or give it to callers or visitors; I offer to connect a call or take a message. I check identity before giving out a replacement key, and I keep registration cards, passports and payment details out of sight and locked away. Keys and key cards are controlled: master keys are signed out and back in, kept on the body and never lent, and lost keys are reported at once so that locks or cards can be changed. Room attendants keep the trolley across the open door, never let anyone into a room without checking with the front desk, and lock doors when they leave. Items found in rooms are logged and handed to lost property. Staff wear their name badges, watch for strangers in staff areas, and report suspicious people or unattended bags to security without touching or confronting them. Cash is kept in a locked drawer or safe, and guests are told about the in-room safe.
markingPoints: Room numbers never said aloud or given out; calls connected or messages taken
Identity checked before keys are given; guest documents kept private and locked away
Key control: master keys signed out, never lent, lost keys reported
Room attendants control who enters rooms; lost property is logged
Suspicious people or items reported to security without confronting them; cash and valuables secured

essays.stem: Describe the personal hygiene rules for food handlers and housekeeping staff, and explain why they matter.
essays.modelAnswer: Good personal hygiene stops germs spreading to food, guests and co-workers. Staff should bathe daily, keep nails short and clean, and wear a clean uniform every shift. Food handlers wear no nail polish, keep their hair tied back and covered, and wear little or no jewellery, because it holds germs and can fall into food. Hands are washed with soap and warm water before work, after using the toilet, after handling raw food, bins, money or chemicals, after coughing or sneezing, and between tasks. Gloves are changed often and do not replace hand washing. In the kitchen, cuts are covered with a blue waterproof plaster. Staff do not eat, smoke or chew gum while handling food. Anyone with diarrhoea, vomiting or a skin infection must tell the supervisor and stay away from food until they are allowed back. Food handlers in Jamaica must hold a Food Handler's Permit from the local health department. Housekeeping staff wash their hands after cleaning toilets or handling dirty linen, before touching clean linen or guest supplies.
markingPoints: Clean body and uniform, short clean nails, hair covered and little jewellery
Hand washing at the right times with soap, and changing gloves often
Cuts covered with blue waterproof plasters; no eating, smoking or gum while handling food
Reports illness and stays away from food until allowed back
Explains why it matters (stops germs reaching food and guests), and mentions the Food Handler's Permit or housekeeping hand washing

essays.stem: Describe how a villa or hotel should prepare for a hurricane, and what staff should do after the storm has passed.
essays.modelAnswer: The hurricane season in Jamaica runs from June to November, so the property should have a written hurricane plan and train staff on it. When a storm is forecast, staff follow the official warnings and the manager's instructions. They bring in or tie down loose items such as pool furniture, umbrellas and plant pots, which can become dangerous in high winds, and fit shutters or board up windows. They check that emergency supplies are ready: drinking water, food that keeps, torches, batteries, first-aid kits, a battery radio and fuel for the generator. Important papers and computers are protected, and guests are told what to expect and where the safe rooms are. Staff also plan for the safety of their own families. After the storm, nobody goes outside until the all-clear is given. Staff then check for hazards before working: fallen power lines (stay well away and report them), gas leaks, broken glass, flooding and damaged roofs. Damage is photographed and reported, and food is checked after a power cut and thrown away if it may be unsafe.
markingPoints: Has a written hurricane plan, and follows official warnings and the manager's instructions
Secures loose items and protects windows
Checks emergency supplies (water, food, torches, first aid, radio, generator fuel) and informs guests
After the storm, waits for the all-clear and checks for hazards such as fallen lines, gas leaks, glass and flooding
Records and reports damage, and checks food after power cuts

essays.stem: Explain how a room attendant should deal safely with broken glass, a used needle and a spill of blood or vomit in a guest room.
essays.modelAnswer: For broken glass, I keep people away, put on thick gloves and pick up the large pieces carefully, then sweep up the small pieces with a dustpan and brush, using a damp paper towel for tiny pieces. I never pick up glass with bare hands or put it loose in a bin bag, where it could cut someone; it goes into a sharps or glass box, or is wrapped well and labelled. For a used needle, I do not touch it with my hands or try to put the cap back on. I use tongs to put it into a sharps container, then report it to the supervisor. If I am pricked, I let the wound bleed gently, wash it with soap and running water, report it at once and get medical advice. For blood or vomit, I put on disposable gloves and an apron, cover the spill with the body-fluid spill kit, scoop it up, clean the area with detergent, then disinfect it as the product label says. The waste goes in a sealed bag, and I wash my hands afterwards.
markingPoints: Broken glass: keeps people away, wears gloves, picks up and sweeps carefully, never with bare hands
Glass put in a sharps or glass box, or wrapped and labelled
Needle: never touched by hand or recapped; tongs into a sharps container; reported
Needle-stick injury: bleed gently, wash, report and get medical advice
Body fluids: gloves and apron, spill kit, clean then disinfect, sealed waste and hand washing

practical1.title: Safety, security and hygiene inspection of a training guest room and kitchen, with a risk assessment
practical1.brief: As a group, carry out a safety, security and hygiene inspection of the Centre's training guest room and bathroom, its training kitchen and the front desk area, then write a short risk assessment. Before you start, the assessor may set up some hazards for you to find, for example an unlabelled spray bottle, a frayed cord with a tag on it, a trolley blocking an exit, a wet floor with no sign, a key left on the desk, or a registration card left in view. Each member inspects one area with the assessor's inspection checklist, and another member checks their findings. For each hazard, write what it is, who could be harmed and how, how high the risk is (low, medium or high) and the control you suggest. Put the simple ones right safely, for example by putting out a wet floor sign, moving the trolley or locking away the key and card, and report the rest to the assessor as you would to a supervisor. Do not touch electrical faults or unknown chemicals: label and report them. Finally, present the risk assessment to the assessor, with each member explaining their own area. Photograph each stage below and add the photos to the group's practical. Hand in the completed checklists and the risk assessment once for the whole group.
materials: Inspection checklists from the assessor, one for each area
Clipboards, pens, and a camera or phone for the photos
Wet floor signs, "Do not use" tags and labels
Rubber gloves and safety glasses for checking the chemical store
photos: The group being briefed and sharing out the areas
Each member inspecting their area with the checklist (one photo per member)
Each hazard found, before it was put right or reported
The simple hazards after they were put right (sign out, exit cleared, key locked away)
The group presenting the risk assessment to the assessor
checklist: Inspected their area carefully, using the checklist
Found and recorded the hazards in their area correctly
Said who could be harmed and how, and rated the risk sensibly
Suggested a suitable control for each hazard
Put simple hazards right safely, and reported electrical faults and unknown chemicals without touching them
Noticed security and privacy risks, such as keys or guest details left in view
Explained their part of the risk assessment clearly to the assessor
safety: Do not touch electrical faults, damaged cords or sockets: tag and report them
Do not open, smell or mix unknown chemicals; wear gloves and glasses in the chemical store
Walk, do not run, and watch for wet floors and trip hazards
Do not climb on furniture to look at high places; use a step ladder only if the assessor allows and someone holds it

practical2.title: Emergency drill and incident report: fire evacuation, burn first aid and a front desk security check
practical2.brief: As a group, carry out three short emergency exercises that the assessor sets, then write an incident report. Exercise 1, fire: when the assessor starts a practice alarm (a whistle or bell, not the building's alarm unless the Centre allows), one member raises the alarm and reads out the fire plan, the group checks the training room and closes the doors, and leads the "guests" (another group or the assessor) by the nearest safe exit to the assembly point, where one member takes a roll call. Back inside, each member points to and names one type of extinguisher and says which fire it is for, and one member shows how to place a fire blanket over a cold, empty pan. Do not set off any extinguisher unless the Centre provides a training extinguisher and the assessor allows it. Exercise 2, first aid: one member plays a cook with a burnt hand (there is no real burn) and another gives the first aid, cooling the "burn" under cool running water and calling the first aider. Exercise 3, security: a person with no ID asks the front desk for a key to a guest room, and one member handles it politely and safely. Each member leads at least one part. Finally, the group completes an incident report for one exercise. Photograph each stage below and add the photos to the group's practical.
materials: A whistle or bell for the practice alarm, and the Centre's fire plan and assembly point map
Fire extinguishers on display (not to be set off unless the Centre provides a training extinguisher), and a fire blanket
A cold, empty pan for the fire blanket demonstration
The Centre's first-aid kit and a sink with running water
A desk set up as a front desk, a mock key and a mock registration card
Blank incident report forms and pens
photos: The group at the assembly point, with the roll call being taken
Each member pointing to and naming an extinguisher type (one photo per member)
The fire blanket being placed over the cold pan
The burn first aid under running water
The front desk security role play
checklist: Raised the alarm or followed the fire plan correctly, without running or using a lift
Helped guide the "guests" out and took part in the roll call
Named an extinguisher type and the fire it is for correctly
